subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should native `openclaw backup create` add exclude patterns now, and which defaults or protected paths are acceptable for secrets and restorability?
rationale: The requested flags are useful and aligned, but the exact defaults, protected backup contents, fail-open/fail-closed behavior, and exclude-file trust model affect both security and restore safety.

options.title: Repair and review the linked native PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 as the canonical path after resolving conflicts, product/security concerns, and real archive proof.

options.title: Narrow to explicit user patterns only
options.body: Ship only repeatable `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` first, leaving smart defaults and protected-path overrides for a later maintainer-sponsored design.

options.title: Keep native backup unchanged for now
options.body: Leave this issue open or close it only after deciding that focused backup products such as Keep My Claw should own this behavior outside core.

recommendation.title: Repair and review the linked native PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 as the canonical path after resolving conflicts, product/security concerns, and real archive proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup retry work from steipete included security and archive-lifetime reasoning, making him the best available routing owner for the security-boundary decision.
